text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD: P0) — GPU node pool 'p-rtx-a100-24g' high memory pressure + repeated CUDA OOMs on nvtask-runner-7. Auto-escalation to eng-oncall. Logs: ```kernel: cudaMemcpyAsync returned CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at kv_cache.c:412
runtime: failed to allocate 7.9GB for tensor cache
container: PID 11234 (model-server) killed by OOM
```

oncall-jay: acked oncall, I'm on it. pulling up pool metrics and recent deploys.

sre-ana: I'm on standby. can you confirm if this is concentrated on a single AZ or multi-AZ?

oncall-jay: looks like 3 hosts in us-west-2a, one spike in us-west-2b. memory consumption trend for kvcache showing gradual climb over 40m.

eng-runtime-lead: last rollout to that pool was kernel-compile v1.4.3 ~ 02:10 UTC (today). tagging @eng-runtime. could be a regression in allocator heuristics.

infra-ops: creating an emergency drain for the most impacted nodes to avoid noisy neighbor cascade. Command I'm running: ```gcloud compute instances update-container nvtask-runner-7 --maintenance-policy TERMINATE && kubectl cordon nvtask-runner-7 && kubectl drain nvtask-runner-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```

oncall-jay: paused scheduling to pool via autoscaler override, setting desired=0 for burst queue to stop new long-context requests.

sre-ana: quick mitigation suggestion: enable fallback routing to 'model-small-v2' for routes hitting high-latency/oom-prone shards. That reduces mem per request and keeps customers alive.

oncall-jay: rolling out fallback traffic rule now (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with canary window 2m. Command: ```rbctl traffic-route set --route embed-prod --fallback model-small-v2 --percent 10```

cust-success-mei: any estimate on customers impacted? I see elevated error rates for two customers (acme-analytics, holo-app). Both on dedicated reserved pools in us-west-2. I can message them after we have ETA.

eng-runtime-lead: pulling allocator logs, seeing repeated "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory" interleaved with "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS" on a different host — possible memory corruption. Reverting kernel-compile v1.4.3 may be safer if rolling back is fast.

oncall-jay: rollback staged?

eng-runtime-lead: rolling back is ~5-7m per node. I'd prefer evacuate -> rollback -> bring back. Starting node rollback job for nvtask-runner-7, nvtask-runner-9, nvtask-runner-11.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by oncall-jay. Escalation to SRE after 10m if no resolution.

sre-ana: I'm starting a live CUDA repro on a paused node to see if we can reproduce without customer traffic. Attaching strace/gdb. If ILLEGAL_ADDRESS reproduces, we'll open a kernel bug.

oncall-jay: added runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-oom - following proactive evacuation steps. Noting that auto-kvcache-evict thresholds were disabled by optimization job earlier today, re-enabling them now.

infra-ops: eviction settings toggled back: ```/etc/redwood/kvcache.conf: evict_threshold=0.85 -> 0.65``` and triggered `systemctl restart redwood-kv-daemon`.

eng-runtime-lead: rollback finished for nvtask-runner-7, marked as healthy under monitoring. Memory stabilizing. One host still showing error spikes (nvtask-runner-11) — continuing investigation.

cust-success-mei: messaging affected customers now: short status update, we have partial mitigation (fallback routing) and we're rolling nodes; will follow up with timeline.

oncall-jay: handing off to @sre-ana for next 30m — please monitor PD and customer comms, escalate to eng-runtime if ILLEGAL_ADDRESS repeats. My shift ending in 20m. :wave:

sre-ana: taking over. created a follow-up runbook comment and pinned log snippets. Also created a PagerDuty note with links to k8s events and nodes: https://pd.internal/incidents/PD123456

eng-runtime-lead: noted potential long-term fix: disable aggressive kv prefetch for large-context sessions and add guardrails to kernel allocator commit size. Filing a ticket: RDW-OPS-1921.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: Incident updated — acknowledged by sre-ana, next escalation in 20m if no resolution.

sre-ana: continuing monitoring; memory stabilized after rollback and evictions but we'll keep fallback routing until morning. marking this as mitigated for now, but not resolved. :white_check_mark:

oncall-jay: thanks team. if anything flares, ping here or escalate PD.

cust-success-mei: updated customers with mitigation and next update ETA 2h.

incident-bot: thread closed for active handling handoff (owner: sre-ana).
